question: Which side reaches the ratified E1 painted-wrap landmark bar while preserving the real run-camera read?
method: Two neutral boards were judged before opening blind-side-key.json. Each board holds the same pulled-main terrain, camera, mount ids, mount transforms, and asset paths; only the landmark bodies and shared pack atlas differ.

reasons: The ruined headframe reads as a four-legged mine structure with a mouth, pulley, rope, repairs, and fallen timber instead of a flat sign frame.
The boiler site and flooded gallery separate into recognizable work systems at the run camera instead of dark boxes.
Paint-derived scratches, ink pockets, soot, rust, and sun-bleached battens remain legible without breaking the E2 county palette.
The crossing gains deck beams, repeated bents, X bracing, a repair plate, and a fallen brace while the rail spine stays readable.
North and south boiler/approach sets now read as distinct battered worksites rather than repeated generic blocks.
The mine spur, tar scars, rubble, drums, ore bins, and broken gate create a fought-over industrial approach without adding gameplay authority.

nonBlockingDebt: The shared evidence lighting still compresses dark faces at the real camera; runtime lighting should be checked after the file replacement is mounted.
The pack-lineup camera overlaps distributed assets and is not a scale comparison; the mounted run-camera row remains the promotion gate.
